catalog_quote: 1966:441: "Ударение связано с долготой: долгий слог обычно является ударным (ӯ́да” [ū́daḥ] 'вы'). Основное ударение чаще всего падает на первый слог или на первый компонент дифтонга. На третий и пятый слоги приходится дополнительное ударение: бо́гӑля̀ 'медведь', би́гӧдй 'росомаха'. Дифференцирующее значение ударения может быть показано на следующих примерах: мо́ди 'я' — моди́ 'плечо'; ба́го 'яма' — баго́ 'бусина'." ... 1966:439: "Настоящая статья написана на материале наречия бай" ... 1966:456 (§19): "Звуковой и грамматический строй обоих наречий, в основном, едины." ... 1993:345 §2.1.2: "Словесное ударение падает преимущественно на первый слог. Гласные в ударной позиции имеют относительно бо́льшую длительность, чем в неударной."

audit.recode_to: Identity first: the deciding sources (Tereščenko 1966, 1993) describe Bai = Forest Enets (fore1265), for which the catalog already has a record coded fixed: initial syllable from Siegl 2013 — so this record is a second, conflicting Forest Enets coding under a Tundra label. If a Tundra Enets record is kept, re-source it to Khanina 2018:433 + Khanina & Shluinsky 2022:185 (predominantly-initial, not fixed, no weight condition stated; 'stress identical in the two Enets') pending Khanina & Shluinsky 2023, i.e. drop the CVV weight condition (weight-hedged -> initial-predominant/hedged, non-quantity-sensitive) unless the 2023 chapter states one.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all four quoted passages are present verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated places (1966 p.441 scanned + page scan; p.439 scope; §19 p.456; 1993 p.345 §2.1.2). (2) Deciding source: a 1966 20-pp handbook sketch (plus the same author's 1993 7-pp sketch); both say in so many words that they are written on Bai-dialect (Forest Enets) material, and the record's Tundra label comes from the StressTyp2 entry for this language, not from the source. The catalog separately codes fore1265 fixed: initial syllable from Siegl 2013, whose §2.11 (held text, p.102) explicitly re-tested Tereščenko 1966:441's non-initial-stress lexemes and found them initially stressed; so the same languoid is coded two ways from two sources. (3) For Tundra Enets itself, Glottolog lists Khanina & Shluinsky 2023 (60 pp, both lects) and Labanauskas 2002 (Madu notes); OpenAlex/CrossRef show the 2023 Routledge and Siegl 2022 Oxford chapters

sources.citation: Khanina, Olesya & Andrey Shluinsky. 2022. Forest Enets and Tundra Enets: How different are they and why? In: Hämeenmaalta Jamalille. Kirja Tapani Salmiselle, 181-200. Helsinki. DOI 10.31885/9789515180858.16 (hdl 10138/342418)
sources.quote: "In both Enets, root morphemes do not allow for closed syllables at the phonological level (except for closed syllables with final /ʔ/) ... Phonetic realization of stress does not display any distinctions in the two Enets either." (i.e. TE stress = FE stress per the current documenters; no weight condition stated)

sources.citation: Khanina, Olesya. 2018. Documenting a language with phonemic and phonetic variation: the case of Enets. Language Documentation & Conservation 12: 430-460.http://hdl.handle.net/10125/24772
sources.quote: "As is typical for Uralic languages, the first syllable is often more prominent in Enets than other syllables: all three stress-related parameters (length, intensity, and pitch) can contribute to prominence. The second syllable can also be prominent; further syllables are rarely prominent ... In short, the situation with Enets stress is very messy and a proper study of stress in Enets is yet to be undertaken. For the moment, it is only clear that there is no easily identifiable fixed stress in Enets, and that the first syllable is more prominent than other syllables more often than not."
sources.locator: p. 433, §1.4 'Summary of Enets phonology' (paper covers both FE and TE; ca. 7 h TE recordings, p. 432)
